Key Finding: In 2024, 34.2% of Eastern Visayas households had internet access at home, placing the region among the six with the lowest household access.
APA Reference: Philippine Statistics Authority. (2025, September 2). Eastern Visayas region: Households’ access to internet (preliminary results) [Infographic]. https://rsso08.psa.gov.ph/system/files/infographics/EV-2024%20NICTHS%20Individual%20and%20HH%20Access.pdf

Key Finding: Jeepney passengers surveyed in Davao City identified poor waiting conditions, long travel times, and inadequate terminals as service problems.
APA Reference: Japan International Cooperation Agency. (2018). Davao City infrastructure development plan and capacity building project: Final report (Vol. 1, Part I, Present situation and annex). https://openjicareport.jica.go.jp/710/710/710_118_12308714.html

Key Finding: Transport disadvantage can compound poverty and social exclusion by limiting access to essential services and economic opportunities.
APA Reference: Lucas, K. (2012). Transport and social exclusion: Where are we now? Transport Policy, 20, 105–113. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tranpol.2012.01.013

Key Finding: Manila used a mobile mapping application and an open data standard to build a route map that supported both passenger trip planning and agency route planning.
APA Reference: World Bank. (2017). Philippines urbanization review: Fostering competitive, sustainable and inclusive cities. https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/963061495807736752/pdf/114088-REVISED-PUBLIC-Philippines-Urbanization-Review-Full-Report.pdf

Key Finding: In urban street-canyon tests, signals arriving without a direct line of sight were the main source of outlying smartphone satellite range measurements.
APA Reference: Weng, D., Hou, Z., Meng, Y., Cai, M., & Chan, Y. (2023). Characterization and mitigation of urban GNSS multipath effects on smartphones. Measurement, 223, Article 113766. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.measurement.2023.113766

Key Finding: The rollout of real-time bus information in New York City was associated with a median 1.7% increase in weekday ridership at the route level.
APA Reference: Brakewood, C., Macfarlane, G. S., & Watkins, K. E. (2015). The impact of real-time information on bus ridership in New York City. Transportation Research Part C: Emerging Technologies, 53, 59–75. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.trc.2015.01.021

Key Finding: British transport studies reviewed by Wardman generally placed a higher value on saving a minute of waiting than on saving a minute spent aboard a vehicle.
APA Reference: Wardman, M. (2004). Public transport values of time. Transport Policy, 11(4), 363–377. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tranpol.2004.05.001

Key Finding: JICA estimated Metro Manila's daily transport costs under congested conditions at ₱3.5 billion in 2017.
APA Reference: Japan International Cooperation Agency. (2018). JICA Philippines annual report 2018: Partners in nation building. https://www.jica.go.jp/english/overseas/philippine/others/__icsFiles/afieldfile/2025/01/31/report_2018.pdf

Key Finding: The 1999 Metro Manila transport review documented jeepney drivers who leased franchised vehicles and depended on fare receipts to cover rent, fuel, and incidental costs.
APA Reference: Japan International Cooperation Agency. (1999). Metro Manila urban transportation integration study: Public transportation (Technical Report No. 9). https://openjicareport.jica.go.jp/710/710/710_118_11580552.html

Key Finding: Typhoons and flooding expose Philippine roads to landslides and embankment erosion, with closures disrupting passenger and goods movement.
APA Reference: World Bank. (2015). Disaster risk management in the transport sector: A review of concepts and international case studies (Vol. 1). https://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/524081468188378328

Key Finding: PAGASA projected more extreme rainfall events in Luzon and the Visayas, with projections varying by region.
APA Reference: Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration. (2011). Climate change in the Philippines. https://pubfiles.pagasa.dost.gov.ph/iaas/ClimateChange_in_the_Philippines_MDGF_Report_2011.pdf

Key Finding: The Philippine inventory put transport greenhouse gas emissions at about 29.4 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent in 2020.
APA Reference: Philippine Climate Change Commission. (2025). Philippines’ first biennial transparency report (BTR) to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) under the Paris Agreement. https://unfccc.int/documents/646250

Key Finding: The national development plan calls for shifting public transport toward consolidated operators and shared fleet management.
APA Reference: National Economic and Development Authority. (2023). Philippine development plan 2023–2028. https://pdp.depdev.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/Philippine-Development-Plan-2023-2028.pdf

Key Finding: The Philippine local route-planning framework assigns local governments responsibility for collecting data and identifying gaps between public transport supply and demand.
APA Reference: DILG–DOTr Joint Memorandum Circular No. 001, Series of 2017 (Phil.). https://region12.dilg.gov.ph/sites/default/files/issuances/DILG-DOTR-JMC2017-01.pdf

Key Finding: DOTr and JICA signed a cooperation agreement in 2024 that targets better service and route planning for fixed-route public utility vehicles in and around Metro Manila.
APA Reference: Japan International Cooperation Agency. (2024, July 17). JICA and DOTr to improve service quality of PUVs towards road decongestion in Mega Manila. https://www.jica.go.jp/english/overseas/philippine/information/press/2024/1545461_53492.html

Key Finding: The Data Privacy Act limits collection to specified legitimate purposes, requires proportional processing, and limits retention to legally recognized needs.
APA Reference: Data Privacy Act of 2012, Republic Act No. 10173, § 11 (Phil.). https://privacy.gov.ph/Data-Privacy-Act/

Key Finding: The Anti-Distracted Driving Act bars specified device activities both while driving and while briefly stopped at a red light, subject to statutory exceptions.
APA Reference: Anti-Distracted Driving Act, Republic Act No. 10913, §§ 4–6 (2016) (Phil.). https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/70326

Key Finding: The Local Government Code authorizes city and municipal councils to regulate tricycle operations and grant local franchises, subject to national transportation guidelines.
APA Reference: Local Government Code of 1991, Republic Act No. 7160, §§ 447, 458 (Phil.). https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra1991/ra_7160_1991.html

Key Finding: In one mobile-network dataset, four location-and-time observations were enough to distinguish 95% of individuals by their mobility records.
APA Reference: de Montjoye, Y.-A., Hidalgo, C. A., Verleysen, M., & Blondel, V. D. (2013). Unique in the crowd: The privacy bounds of human mobility. Scientific Reports, 3, Article 1376. https://doi.org/10.1038/srep01376

Key Finding: The NIST Privacy Framework recommends minimizing personal data in audit logs and testing the technical controls that govern data processing.
APA Reference: National Institute of Standards and Technology. (2020). NIST privacy framework: A tool for improving privacy through enterprise risk management, version 1.0 (NIST CSWP 10). https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.CSWP.10

Key Finding: A transport equity framework calls for assessing access to essential destinations and whether policies improve opportunities for disadvantaged groups.
APA Reference: Pereira, R. H. M., Schwanen, T., & Banister, D. (2017). Distributive justice and equity in transportation. Transport Reviews, 37(2), 170–191. https://doi.org/10.1080/01441647.2016.1257660
